cases.title: Theft from a locked shop — Shivaji Market
cases.summary: Reported occurrence at Shivaji Market. Theft from a locked shop. Thorough investigation required; the schedule was known in advance, which suggests inside involvement.

cases.title: The Marol Depot Road Payroll Robbery
cases.summary: A payroll van carrying the weekly wages of a logistics firm was waylaid on Marol Depot Road. The security escort was struck down and the cash bag taken. The cashier is unhurt and the guard is in hospital. The company wants it treated as a simple highway robbery.

legalRefs.title: Prohibition and punishment for contravention involving narcotics
legalRefs.plain: The narcotics law, separate from the BNS. Quantity seized decides the severity band.
legalRefs.in_game: Tier 5 branch. The quantity recovered (a lab-weighed fact) sets the punishment band, so the seizure and weighing protocol must be perfect.

legalRefs.title: Damage to computer resource / computer related offences
legalRefs.plain: Hacking and data offences sit under the IT Act alongside BNS cheating.
legalRefs.in_game: Cyber branch charging: BNS s.318 plus IT Act sections for the intrusion itself.

legalRefs.title: Requirements for accidents and vehicle identification
legalRefs.plain: Road accident reporting and vehicle tracing duties.
legalRefs.in_game: Roadside scene branch: chassis/engine number and ANPR tracing feed identity proof.

legalRefs.title: Punishment for murder
legalRefs.plain: Murder carries the heaviest penalty; the framing must be exact.
legalRefs.in_game: Available in the Charge Sheet offence picker for the homicide branch. Over-charging it on a weaker set of facts hurts you.

legalRefs.title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
legalRefs.plain: A lesser homicide charge than murder — used where the intention is not fully established.
legalRefs.in_game: The "partial conviction" path: if your proof supports the lesser charge, this is what the court convicts under instead of acquitting.

legalRefs.title: Voluntarily causing hurt
legalRefs.plain: The basic assault charge.
legalRefs.in_game: Used in the assault branch and as a lesser included offence.

legalRefs.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
legalRefs.plain: A more serious assault charge where the injury is grievous.
legalRefs.in_game: Depends on the medical report grading the injury — a lab dependency.

legalRefs.title: Theft
legalRefs.plain: Taking someone's property without consent is theft.
legalRefs.in_game: Tier 1 branch. The FIR classifier expects the ingredients of dishonest intention and movable property.

legalRefs.title: Robbery
legalRefs.plain: Theft with force or threat of immediate force becomes robbery — a serious charge.
legalRefs.in_game: Tier 2 branch; escalates the day limit to 90 days and raises the standard of proof.

legalRefs.title: Criminal breach of trust
legalRefs.plain: Someone trusted with property took it for themselves.
legalRefs.in_game: Financial branch; depends on document examination and account forensics.

legalRefs.title: Cheating
legalRefs.plain: Lying to someone to get their property or their consent.
legalRefs.in_game: Cyber and financial branches; pairs with s.316 and digital evidence.

legalRefs.title: Criminal conspiracy
legalRefs.plain: An agreement to commit a crime is itself an offence.
legalRefs.in_game: Narcotics and organised branches. Charging conspiracy without evidence of AGREEMENT (meetings, calls, money flow) is the classic over-charge.

legalRefs.title: Possession of counterfeit currency / instruments
legalRefs.plain: Counterfeit money and the tools to make it are separate offences.
legalRefs.in_game: Counterfeit branch; document examination and fingerprint tests.

legalRefs.title: Information in cognizable cases — the FIR
legalRefs.plain: This is the birth of a case. If someone reports a serious (cognizable) crime, you MUST write it down, read it back to them, get their signature, and hand them a free copy. If you wrongly refuse, the complainant can go over your head to the SP.
legalRefs.in_game: In the Duty Room you author the FIR narrative. The classifier checks it against the statutory ingredients of the offence. If you refuse to register a genuine cognizable offence, the complainant escalates to the SP and you lose Standing.

legalRefs.title: Preliminary inquiry before registering an FIR
legalRefs.plain: For middle-weight offences you may ask your SP for permission to spend up to 14 days checking whether there is really a case before you formally register it. It does NOT apply to the gravest offences.
legalRefs.in_game: When the complaint is borderline, you may choose "Seek preliminary inquiry" instead of registering. It buys clarity but costs 14 days off your clock and can look like delay. Choosing wrongly is a scored decision.

legalRefs.title: Inspection of the scene of occurrence
legalRefs.plain: For serious offences you must physically inspect the scene yourself and record your inspection.
legalRefs.in_game: Act 2 gating: the Crime Scene desk requires the arrival log, walk-through and scene diagram before exhibits can be lawfully collected.

legalRefs.title: Inquest by police
legalRefs.plain: For suspicious deaths, police hold a formal inquest and send the body for post-mortem.
legalRefs.in_game: The Inquest step appears in Act 2 on the homicide branch. Completing it unlocks the post-mortem report as a lab item.

legalRefs.title: When may police arrest without a warrant
legalRefs.plain: Arrest without warrant is permitted for cognizable offences, but you must have reasonable suspicion — not a hunch.
legalRefs.in_game: The arrest action in Act 5 is gated on the arrest-legality check. Arresting without recorded reasonable suspicion is a procedural violation that reduces your Standing and hands the defence an argument.

legalRefs.title: Requirement of grounds for arrest
legalRefs.plain: You cannot arrest casually. You must write down WHY the arrest was necessary.
legalRefs.in_game: The Arrest Card requires you to type your grounds. The Legal Arbiter scores the entered grounds against the necessity test.

legalRefs.title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds and right to bail
legalRefs.plain: Inform the arrested person why he is being arrested and that he can seek bail.
legalRefs.in_game: Arrest Card field. Leaving it blank creates a "procedural illegality" flag used against you in court.

legalRefs.title: Search and seizure — independent witnesses
legalRefs.plain: When you seize anything, two independent local witnesses must watch and sign the seizure list.
legalRefs.in_game: THE most important handling rule in the game. A seizure memo with fewer than two witnesses sets exhibits.seizure_valid = 0, which taints the exhibit permanently. Witnesses typed into the memo are validated (not duplicated, not police).

legalRefs.title: Charge sheet and the 60/90 day clock
legalRefs.plain: You have 60 or 90 days to finish investigating and file your report. Miss it and the accused walks out on default bail.
legalRefs.in_game: The HUD day-counter IS this section. Every action burns days. Interrogation, lab requests, surveillance all draw from the same clock. Exceeding day_limit closes the case as a default-bail failure.

legalRefs.title: Report of Police Officer on completion of investigation
legalRefs.plain: This is the charge sheet — the formal document that asks the court to try your accused. It must contain the parties, the case, your witnesses, the offence, and your annexures.
legalRefs.in_game: The Charge Sheet Composer replicates this structure field-for-field. Missing annexures or a wrong accused list are blocking defects.

legalRefs.title: Further investigation
legalRefs.plain: Even after filing, you may keep investigating and file more evidence.
legalRefs.in_game: Unlocked at higher ranks: you may reopen a closed case from the Case Wall if new evidence exists, for a time cost.

legalRefs.title: Cognizance of offences by Magistrate
legalRefs.plain: The court decides whether to accept your charge sheet and take up the case.
legalRefs.in_game: Submitting your charge sheet triggers the cognizance check. A charge sheet with no admissible proof is rejected and returned for further investigation.

legalRefs.title: Examination of accused
legalRefs.plain: The court asks the accused to explain the evidence against him. This is the step where your proof must speak for itself.
legalRefs.in_game: Act 8 stage. If your admissible evidence is thin, the accused simply denies everything and the doubt remains.

legalRefs.title: Summons to produce documents or things
legalRefs.plain: You can formally require a bank, telecom or shop to hand over records.
legalRefs.in_game: Backs the CDR/financial/subpoena actions in Act 4: proper process raises the reliability of the pull.

legalRefs.title: Confession to police officer not provable — the discovery rule
legalRefs.plain: What the accused TELLS you is worthless in court. But if what he tells you leads you to recover a real object or fact, then just that part — the part that led to the discovery — becomes evidence.
legalRefs.in_game: The single most important interrogation mechanic. Confessions are auto-filed as INADMISSIBLE. Only facts you convert into a witnessed RECOVERY survive. The Interrogation Room shows the split live.

legalRefs.title: Chain of custody / continuous possession
legalRefs.plain: You must be able to show the object passed hand to hand without a gap or a chance to tamper.
legalRefs.in_game: Every exhibit carries a custody log. A missing hand-off, or an unlogged transfer, sets custody_intact = 0 and makes the exhibit contestable in court. The Lab Desk and Malkhana steps append to this log.

legalRefs.title: Admissibility of electronic records — the certificate
legalRefs.plain: Digital proof needs a special certificate (the s.63 certificate) signed by two people. Without it, the court will not even look at your CCTV, CDR or phone data.
legalRefs.in_game: Digital exhibits must be hashed AND carry a dual-signed s.63 certificate before the Charge Sheet will accept them. The Cyber Cell operative or FSL digital-forensics expert signs. Missing certificate = inadmissible = cannot be listed.

legalRefs.title: Electronic records as documents
legalRefs.plain: Digital evidence is not weak evidence — but it must be certified.
legalRefs.in_game: Supports the digital branch: a properly certified CCTV clip is high-weight evidence and carries real convictions.

legalRefs.title: Opinion of expert — digital forensics
legalRefs.plain: A qualified expert may give an opinion on technical matters.
legalRefs.in_game: The FSL report carries an expert name and a skill-derived confidence. A low-skilled team produces low-confidence reports; a high-skill team can also SPOT overreach in a report.

legalRefs.title: Opinion as to handwriting, finger impressions
legalRefs.plain: Handwriting and fingerprint experts may opine on identity.
legalRefs.in_game: Backs the Document Examination and Fingerprint lab tests; their reports feed the TIP and identity branch.

legalRefs.title: Relevancy of facts forming part of the same transaction
legalRefs.plain: Facts happening in the same event as the crime are relevant even if not the crime itself.
legalRefs.in_game: Influence the Legal Arbiter: connected circumstances you have recorded raise the coherence of your narrative and the survivability of circumstantial cases.

legalRefs.title: Facts necessary to explain or introduce relevant facts
legalRefs.plain: Facts that give context — who is who, when and where — are relevant.
legalRefs.in_game: Justifies the Identification Parade (TIP) step: identity evidence is admitted under this head.

legalRefs.title: Presumption as to certain offences / abetment
legalRefs.plain: Some facts can be presumed from surrounding circumstances.
legalRefs.in_game: Narcotics and conspiracy branches lean on this; it rewards a properly assembled circumstantial file.

forms.title: Seizure / Recovery Memo
forms.when_used: Whenever anything is taken into custody from a scene, person or premises.
forms.fields_json:
[{"field":"Memo Number & Date","guidance":"Sequential. Never back-date.","required":1},
   {"field":"Place of search / seizure","guidance":"Exact address and, for a scene, the grid reference of the found location.","required":1},
   {"field":"Time of commencement and conclusion","guidance":"Recorded to the minute, both entries.","required":1},
   {"field":"List of items seized","guidance":"Describe each item so it is identifiable years later — make, model, colour, condition, quantity, pack size.","required":1},
   {"field":"Independent Witness 1","guidance":"An adult resident of the locality, not a police officer, not a party to the case.","required":1},
   {"field":"Independent Witness 2","guidance":"A second, different, independent person. Two witnesses is a statutory minimum, not a target.","required":1},
   {"field":"Packing / sealing details","guidance":"How each item was packed, sealed and labelled. Enables the chain of custody to begin cleanly.","required":1},
   {"field":"Signature of IO and witnesses","guidance":"All three sign the same sheet at the same time.","required":1}]
forms.pitfalls: The many ways to lose an exhibit forever: only one witness; a witness who is a police officer; the same person entered twice; no grid reference; a vague description that could be anything; back-dating. Any of these taints the exhibit and it can never be repaired.

snapshot.title: Theft from a locked shop — Shivaji Market
snapshot.summary: Reported occurrence at Shivaji Market. Theft from a locked shop. Thorough investigation required; the schedule was known in advance, which suggests inside involvement.

fir.narrative: Nitin Bhonsle, Account Cashier, Sunrise Logistics Pvt Ltd withdrew cash ₹418000, mostly in ₹500 denominations, on Monday Morning. While transporting the cash to Sector 9, he, alongwith Mr. Ramzan, was stopped by two armed unknown men around Marol Depot Road. Mr. Ramzan was hit by the gun on head which caused head injury and visible external bleeding. The victims claim it to be a planned robbery by unknown persons.

transcript.text: Saab, I was at home, with my family. Where else would I be? I didn't go anywhere that morning.

transcript.text: Who did you lend the vehicle to, and on what date?

transcript.text: What vehicle, Saab? I don't even own a vehicle, let alone lend one to someone. I told you, I was at home that morning, with my family.
